clue.text: Son volunteers to help around the grounds

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word for help round so it reads backwards

parts.note: to help is to aid

explanation.surface: A son pitches in with volunteers who tidy up the grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns AID into DIA. The TA (Territorial Army) is the British Army's volunteer reserve, a crossword staple for 'volunteers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is the Latin-style plural of stadium, and sports grounds are stadiums.

clue.text: Barrel that is housing pet, a sea creature

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

indicators.note: housing means the letters for that is enclose the pet

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates Latin id est, that is
a cat is a household pet

explanation.surface: A barrel turns out to be home to a pet sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunicate, or sea squirt, is a marine invertebrate with a tough outer tunic.

clue.text: Reserve one's seat at last in the ballet?

indicators.note: in says the pieces go inside the word for the ballet

parts.note: ballet is an example of dance, which the question mark flags
one is I, so one's gives I'S

indicators.note: at last takes only the final letter of the word seat

explanation.surface: Book your seat at the ballet before they run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a booking verb but is the noun meaning aloofness; 'the ballet?' is dance by example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance in the sense of coolness or aloofness is a synonym of reserve in manner.

clue.text: High point surrounded by a grassy area in South American region

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the high point inside the following letters

parts.note: a llano is a grassy plain in South America
a tip is the top or peak of something

explanation.surface: A peak surrounded by grassland in a South American region.
explanation.walkthrough: A llano is a Spanish word for the tropical grassy plains of Venezuela and Colombia, familiar in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The Altiplano is the high Andean plateau of Bolivia and Peru.

clue.text: Got going, though not initially well turned out?

indicators.note: not initially says the phrase loses its opening letter

parts.note: got going means started up, as an engine does

explanation.surface: Someone got going, though they didn't start out looking smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' drops the S from STARTED UP. The question mark flags that a dressed-up look is only arguably 'well turned out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarted up is British slang for dressed up showily, so a person so treated is, loosely, smartly turned out.

clue.text: Student's last studies: love, in Shakespeare's O plays

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word student

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: in puts the love score inside the next phrase

parts.note: Shakespeare is the Bard, so Shakespeare's is the Bard's
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A student's final reading is the love interest in Shakespeare's plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' looks like nouns for Shakespeare's works but is the verb, to act on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread the boards is an idiom for acting on stage, so it fits plays as a verb.

clue.text: Family of statesmen, say, in terrible S situation

indicators.note: say means the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: the Pitts, father and son, were both British prime ministers

explanation.surface: A great political family finds itself in a dire position.
explanation.walkthrough: William Pitt the Elder and his son William Pitt the Younger were both 18th-century British prime ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: The pits is informal for the worst possible situation.

clue.text: Buttoning up letter, girlfriend is to set off

indicators.note: buttoning means the girlfriend's word fastens round the letter

parts.note: a date is someone you go out with

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for letter is read backwards

parts.note: a note is a short letter

explanation.surface: A girlfriend fastening her coat over a letter is about to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the letter into ETON; 'Buttoning' pictures the girlfriend fastened round it, a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate is to set off an explosive.

clue.text: Roman Catholic using Indian language in former times

indicators.note: in places the language inside the word for former times

parts.note: the past is former times
Pali is the ancient Indian language of Buddhist scripture

explanation.surface: A Catholic uses an old Indian tongue in bygone days.
explanation.definitionFit: A papalist is a supporter of the Pope and papal authority, typically a Roman Catholic.

clue.text: Tisane replaced by tea, not a liqueur

indicators.note: replaced says the letters of the herbal drink and what follows are put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not means the letter a is left out of the word tea

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instead of a herbal infusion, someone serves tea rather than a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' removes A from TEA, leaving TE; 'replaced' then rearranges TISANE plus TE into the liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur, an example of the class.

clue.text: Tabloid journalist to face pressure after start of rumour

indicators.note: after says the journalist and what follows come behind the letter from rumour
start of picks out just the opening letter of the word rumour

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crosswords' usual journalist
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A tabloid hack must face the pressure that follows a whiff of rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' is a link here. A red top is a British downmarket tabloid, named for the red mastheads of papers like The Sun and the Mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-top is British slang for a sensationalist popular newspaper, named after its red masthead.

clue.text: Fought: that is, used knuckles

parts.note: sc., short for Latin scilicet, means that is or namely
to rap is to knock with the knuckles

explanation.surface: They fought, that is to say they used their knuckles.
explanation.walkthrough: SC (scilicet) is a scholarly abbreviation for 'that is'; the surface's 'knuckles' suggests a fist fight but means knocking on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap is informal for to fight or brawl, so having scrapped is having fought.

clue.text: Outstanding film director is making comeback

indicators.note: making comeback says the director's name and the following word are read backwards

parts.note: Fritz Lang was the director of Metropolis
taken as written

explanation.surface: An outstanding film director is returning to the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' turns LANG IS into SIGNAL; Fritz Lang made Metropolis and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means striking or notable, as in a signal achievement.

clue.text: Plan brief residence in French city

parts.note: a chart is a map or plan
res is the common short form of residence

explanation.surface: Someone maps out a short stay in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres is a cathedral city in northern France, southwest of Paris.

clue.text: Next cases to be treated with precision

indicators.note: to be treated means the letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: The next patients must be seen to with great care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be treated' rearranges the nine letters of NEXT CASES.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness is accuracy or precision, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Her Excellency is, according to some yokels, a goddess

parts.note: HE stands for His or Her Excellency, an ambassador's title
in rustic dialect be is used for is, as in 'that be right'

explanation.surface: The ambassador's wife, country folk say, is divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yokels' signals regional dialect, where 'be' stands in for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe was the Greek goddess of youth and cupbearer to the gods.

clue.text: Henry cut up, at school, a class of insects

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to axe is to cut
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: Henry was beaten up at school, a victim of insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AXE into EXA; 'school' looks like a classroom but is a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: Hexapoda is the taxonomic class of six-legged arthropods, the insects.

clue.text: Chancellor once announced business target

indicators.note: announced means the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: biz is slang for business, and a target is a mark

explanation.surface: A firm announces its business goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Otto von Bismarck was the first Chancellor of the German Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Bismarck was Germany's Iron Chancellor in the late nineteenth century.

clue.text: Secretary with little time for religious faction

parts.note: T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A secretary has hardly a moment for a breakaway church.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a group that has split from a larger religious body, a faction.

clue.text: Ears could be one's asset

definitions.meaning: ears of grain kept back for planting next season
figuratively, a resource set aside to bring future gains

explanation.definitionFit: Seedcorn is grain saved for sowing, and figuratively any asset kept for future returns.

clue.text: From employee in casino I procure change

indicators.note: change says the letters are altered into another order

explanation.surface: A casino worker says, I get the change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges I PROCURE; it hints at casino chips, but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier is the casino employee who runs a gaming table.

clue.text: One hundred: — too old for insurance

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred
overage means beyond the permitted age

explanation.surface: At a hundred you are far too old to get insured.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a centenarian refused a policy; the stray colon and dash are newspaper print marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the protection an insurance policy provides, so it stands for insurance itself.

clue.text: Thespian group's performing: gets first row in stitches call

parts.note: a cast is a group of actors, so the cast's
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: An acting company performs and has the front row in stitches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in stitches' suggests laughter, but the definition is about knitting: casting on makes the first row of stitches.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast on in knitting is to put the first row of loops on the needle.

clue.text: Bulk of television viewers maybe offered a fourth-rate service?

parts.note: D is the fourth grade after A, B and C
Mass is the Catholic church service

explanation.surface: A fourth-rate church service might be offered to the mass of TV viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks TV viewers as one example of the mass audience advertising targets.
explanation.definitionFit: Admass is the section of the public swayed by mass advertising, of which TV audiences are the prime example.

clue.text: Old boy, wearing sulky expression, ceased to be involved

indicators.note: the sulky face wears the boy, so his name goes inside it

parts.note: a pout is a sulky look
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: An old boy with a sulky face withdrew from the activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' works in reverse of the surface: the sulky expression wears the boy, so TED sits inside rather than outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to choose to withdraw from taking part, to stop being involved.

clue.text: Terrifying woman moved on, abandoning extremes

indicators.note: abandoning extremes means the ends are stripped away, here two letters from each end

parts.note: to move on is to progress, so moved on is progressed

explanation.surface: A frightening woman moved on, giving up her extreme views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning extremes' strips PR from the front and ED from the back of PROGRESSED; taking two letters at each end is looser than the usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female ogre, a monster of fairy tales, hence a frightening woman.

clue.text: Somehow chorister hasn't succeeded in the art of public speaking

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the singer are rearranged after one is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A choirboy somehow failed to master oratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't' removes S, the genealogists' abbreviation for succeeded, from CHORISTER; the indicator 'Somehow' then rearranges the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive speaking or writing, oratory.

clue.text: State troops going after a criminal nark

indicators.note: going after places the troops behind the earlier letters
criminal suggests the informer's letters are corrupted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the SAS, Special Air Service, are British special forces troops

explanation.surface: Troops go after a crooked police informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges NARK into RKAN; a nark is British slang for a police informer, and the SAS is the British Army's special forces regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is a state of the southern United States.

clue.text: One way to preserve tomatoes of various kinds

definitions.meaning: tomatoes can be dried in the sunshine to keep them

explanation.surface: A recipe tip about keeping tomatoes in assorted varieties.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundry means assorted or miscellaneous; read as sun-dry it is drying food in the sun.
